Finally, we illustrate the use of correlative statistical methods to assess and predict the occurrence of microstructural anomalies (e.g., abnormal grain growth) and report on progress in the creation and curation of microstructural repositories that facilitate data sharing. The aim of this Overview is to make the case that ML tools have become, in a relatively short time, indispensible aids for microstructural image processing and interpretation.

title: Machine learning insights into microstructural origins of transport and mechanical properties in porous microstructures
abstract: Multifunctional porous materials are increasingly needed across various fields, but their complex microstructures create significant challenges due to the intricate microstructure-property relationships. This complexity, combined with limitations of traditional analysis methods, hinders efforts to understand and optimize microstructure–property relationships. To address this, we integrate physics-based mesoscale modeling with interpretable machine learning (ML) to uncover how microstructural features govern effective diffusivity and elastic modulus. At constant porosity, we show diffusivity varies by over 150 × and modulus by ∼50 ×, highlighting the power of microstructure engineering. Statistical analysis reveals bimodal behavior in diffusivity and unimodal in modulus. ML identifies connectivity as the dominant factor, while modulus is also sensitive to domain size and feature interactions. Controlled simulations further highlight domain shape as a critical feature for modulus. This framework enables efficient exploration of microstructure-property correlations, offering new insights to guide the design of advanced porous materials.

title: Data-selective machine learning framework (DSML) for defect-aware, interpretable yield-strength prediction for LPBF-fabricated AlSi10Mg alloys
abstract: The yield strength of laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) alloys remains challenging to predict owing to defect-driven variability that cannot be captured by conventional near-dense empirical equations. Here, we develop a data-selective machine learning (DSML) pipeline that integrates data-driven black-box modeling with physics-informed white-box modeling through symbolic regression to derive a defect-aware, interpretable closed-form equation. A dual-source dataset was constructed, including 44 fully labeled datasets (process parameters, microstructural features, and mechanical properties), and 111 process-only datasets containing porosity data. The DSML framework identifies critical descriptors and then embeds a porosity sub-model into a closed-form yield-strength equation, explicitly capturing the influence of process-induced defects. Validation was performed via AlSi10Mg fabricated using LPBF under six distinct conditions. The results revealed that the porosity-aware white-box model achieves a coefficient of determination of 0.90 and mean absolute error (MAE) of 9.51 MPa, outperforming both the black-box predictor and a widely used cell-size–based empirical relation (MAE = 41.98 MPa). The recovered terms align with known mechanisms (effective load-bearing reduction by pores and boundary-mediated strengthening) and preserve dimensional consistency, enabling the construction of process–design maps for defect-aware optimization. By internalizing defect effects in an interpretable equation and performing rigorous validation against independent experimental conditions, this work provides a reproducible, physics-consistent route to determining process–structure–property relationships for LPBF AlSi10Mg and a scalable foundation for incorporating additional strengthening mechanisms in next-generation LPBF materials.

title: Data-driven design of Nb-W refractory alloys using Transformer-based stress-strain modeling
abstract: Generative AI provides a powerful route for predicting material behavior in data-scarce regimes, an especially pressing challenge for refractory alloys where extreme processing environments and high melting points hinder large-scale data collection. Here, we introduce a Transformer-based generative framework that models the entire deformation trajectory rather than focusing solely on isolated scalar properties (such as YS, UTS), by synthesizing full stress–strain curves of Nb-W-based refractory alloys. Applied to Nb521-derived systems, the model captures the sequential evolution of tensile deformation and accurately predicts elastic–plastic responses across a wide compositional and processing space. The framework demonstrates utility in three downstream tasks: (i) inverse design of composition and processing, yielding >35% strength improvement without loss of ductility; (ii) interpretable regime analysis via a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) mechanism, highlighting the beneficial roles of Hf and Ta in ductility, consistent with experimental and DFT validation; and (iii) seamless integration of generated curves into finite element simulations for structural performance assessment. Together, these results establish a coherent generative-analytic-predictive workflow for mechanism-aware, data-efficient design of advanced refractory alloys.

title: Revealing cryo-loading induced twinning and its impact on titanium via correlative data-driven mechanomicroscopy
abstract: Twinning plays a pivotal role in strengthening titanium and its alloys, particularly at cryogenic temperatures, yet the factors controlling twin evolution and associated hardening mechanisms remain largely elusive. To tackle this problem, we combine electron backscattered diffraction (EBSD) with site-specific high-resolution nanoindentation mapping to correlatively investigate the cryogenically rolled titanium with tailored grain sizes, leveraging machine learning for large-scale data analysis. Characterization of ∼8000 twins confirms the existence of four types of twins in the deformed sample where {101¯2} twins and {112¯2} twins are the predominant ones. Twin density scales positively with grain size, as larger grains accommodate more twins and diverse variants. Grain orientation further governs twin selection and intragranular area fraction via the effective rolling Schmid factor. Correlative nanoindentation-EBSD mapping reveals that twinned regions outperform equiaxed grains in hardness, independent of orientation effects. Machine learning of these datasets delineates a hardening hierarchy of {112¯2} secondary twins > 112¯2 primary twins > {101¯2} twins>matrix. Dislocation characterization within twin regions indicates that the high hardening capacity of twins is attributed to the 〈c + a〉 dislocations in twins. These insights unravel the interplay of grain size, orientation, and twinning in cryogenic deformation, furnishing a microstructure-driven framework for optimizing mechanical performance of titanium alloys.

title: Predicting grain boundary void nucleation sites in microstructure during shock loading with convolutional neural networks
abstract: Void nucleation in ductile materials subjected to high strain-rate loading remains a critical yet elusive phenomenon to understand. Traditional methods to understand void nucleation typically rely on experiments and molecular dynamics and do not capture the underlying factors leading to void nucleation. In this study, a convolutional neural network, specifically a U-Net enhanced with attention gates, is developed to predict void nucleation probability in pristine tantalum microstructures. The approach leverages a multi-channel input, incorporating four channels of grain orientations and an additional channel of grain boundary energy calculated via the lattice matching method. Void nucleation probability fields are determined from post-mortem micrographs and serve as ground truth, distinguishing void from no-void regions at the pixel level. Pixel-level class imbalance, common in such images, is addressed by using focal loss to guide the network’s training to predict void nucleation sites more effectively. The model not only predicts void nucleation sites consistent with ground-truth but also reveals additional potential void nucleation sites. Analysis of the trained model reveals the nuanced interaction between the visible and invisible channels, indicating its ability to learn complex relationships between microstructure and properties. Even with relatively limited training data, this work shows that CNN-based models can predict void nucleation sites while considering combined interplay of factors such as grain boundary energy and grain orientation. In this way, machine learning can serve as a means to understand the underlying factors leading to void nucleation thereby contributing to a fundamental understanding of failure due to spallation in ductile materials.

title: Evaluation of micro-mechanical behavior for low carbon-containing alumina refractory assisted by interpretable machine learning: toward development of digital materials
abstract: Carbon-containing alumina refractories are important materials of several functional metallurgical components, and their service performance is ruled by their micro-scale mechanical behavior. By integrating nano-indentation testing with interpretable machine learning, an experimental-computational workflow comprising probabilistic microstructural clustering and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-guided Tabular Prior-Fitting Network (TabPFN) modeling was established. The study quantitatively identifies the micro-scale functional clusters and corresponding unified microstructural states with the proportion and influence score. A correlation between micro- and macro-mechanical behavior is demonstrated. Additionally, the effects of replacement of 10% flake graphite by 1% expanded graphite as well as the impact of thermal shock on the microstructure and properties evolution are clearly interpreted based on the key feature selection. The processing-microstructure-property integrated material model and methodology established in this study bridge micromechanical mechanisms and macroscopic performance, offering an interpretable basis for the development of heterogeneous digital refractory.

title: Uncertainty-aware machine learning framework for predicting dislocation plasticity and stress–strain response in metallic alloys, Part II: BCC systems
abstract: There is increasing interest in using artificial intelligence (AI) to accelerate alloy design. However, most AI models for alloy design remain deterministic and often struggle to reconcile the scatter, sparsity, and incompleteness typical of experimental mechanical-property datasets. Here, we present an uncertainty-aware, physics-informed probabilistic framework to predict dislocation plasticity and full stress–strain response distributions in body-centered cubic (BCC) metals and alloys using limited tensile data available in the literature. We first calibrate the generalized size-dependent Taylor strengthening (GS-DTS) model for BCC systems using Bayesian regression, producing probabilistic estimates of the BCC strengthening coefficients. We then train a Gaussian process regression (GPR) model to learn the dislocation density evolution as a function of strain and key microstructural descriptors, providing both mean predictions and calibrated uncertainty estimates. Embedding this probabilistic dislocation-density model within a representative polycrystalline framework enables the prediction of the stress–strain response as probability bands rather than single deterministic curves. The framework is validated against experimental stress–strain data for Nb, V, Mo, and α-Fe, and is further applied to the refractory high-entropy alloys HfNbTaTiZr and NbTiZr. These results demonstrate transferability beyond the initial training set when dislocation-mediated plasticity dominates. Finally, we separate model uncertainty from input uncertainty and show that solute interaction energies and solute concentrations are dominant contributors to prediction uncertainty. Overall, this approach converts uncertainty into actionable information for experiment planning, model reliability assessment, and mechanism-aware exploration of BCC alloy design space.

title: Machine learning-driven creep law discovery across alloy compositional space
abstract: High-temperature creep characterization of structural alloys traditionally relies on serial uniaxial tests, which are highly inefficient for exploring the large search space of alloy compositions and for material discovery. Here, we introduce a machine-learning-assisted, high-throughput framework for creep law identification based on a dimple array bulge instrument (DABI) configuration, which enables parallel creep testing of 25 dimples, each fabricated from a different alloy, in a single experiment. Full-field surface displacements of dimples undergoing time-dependent creep-induced bulging under inert gas pressure are measured by 3D digital image correlation. We train a recurrent neural network as a surrogate model, mapping creep parameters and loading conditions to the time-dependent deformation response of DABI. Coupling this surrogate with a particle swarm optimization scheme enables rapid and global inverse identification with sparsity regularization of creep parameters from experimental displacement–time histories. In addition, we propose a phenomenological creep law with a time-dependent stress exponent that captures the sigmoidal primary creep observed in wrought INCONEL 625 and extracts its temperature dependence from DABI tests at multiple temperatures. Furthermore, we employ a general creep law combining several conventional forms with regularized inversion to identify the creep laws for 47 additional Fe-, Ni-, and Co-rich alloys and to automatically select the dominant functional form for each alloy. This workflow, combined with the DABI experiment, provides a quantitative, high-throughput creep characterization platform that is compatible with data mining, composition–property modeling, and nonlinear structural optimization with creep behavior across a large alloy design space.

title: Electrostatic levitation processing and deep learning investigation of liquid W-Zr refractory alloys
abstract: The competitive nucleation mechanism, crystal growth kinetics and solute diffusion dynamics in undercooled liquid W-Zr refractory alloys were investigated by comparing hyperperitectic W-50Zr, hypoeutectic W-64Zr, and eutectic W-80Zr alloys through electrostatic levitation experiments and deep learning computations. In hyperperitectic W-50Zr alloy, the peritectic transition was suppressed at moderate undercoolings, resulting in the partial retention of the primary (W) phase. When further undercooled beyond a critical threshold of about 280 K, the nucleation rate of W2Zr surpassed that of (W) phase, enabling its direct formation from the undercooled alloy. A discontinuity in the crystal growth velocity with respect to undercooling was observed at this threshold, corresponding to the transformation of the primary phase from (W) to W2Zr phase. In both hyperperitectic W-50Zr and hypoeutectic W-64Zr alloys, a gradient of solute W content formed in the residual liquid after the growth of primary or peritectic W2Zr phase. This gradient is attributed to the low transport mobility of W atoms, with a diffusion coefficient of 5.15×10−9 m2·s−1 determined through non-equilibrium molecular dynamics employing a deep neural network interatomic potential. In these three alloys, the significantly higher nucleation rate of (βZr) phase compared to W2Zr during eutectic transition promoted its preferential formation and increased its volume fraction at high undercoolings.

title: PolyMicros: A foundation model for polycrystalline material structure
abstract: Foundation Models for Materials Science promise the state-of-the-art performance achieved by deep learning techniques on tasks such as microstructure reconstruction and inverse material design, while claiming to avoid large data requirements and time consuming preparation for these specialized tasks. This respite is significant when, for example, studying polycrystalline microstructures where challenging tasks are plentiful but “large” microstructural datasets comprise of single digit examples. However, in practice, current frameworks still require (1) large, multi-million sample pre-training datasets and (2) further fine-tuning to specialize the model to solve down stream tasks of interest. We introduce a novel foundation model approach designed specifically for data sparse, structural materials science applications. For (1), we introduce a physics-driven data augmentation scheme that coordinates an ensemble of local diffusion models to generate a large-scale, physically diverse synthetic dataset. For (2), we demonstrate that a foundation model built using an unconditional diffusion model backbone can be specialized to downstream tasks without fine-tuning. We utilize this framework to construct PolyMicros, the first Foundation model for polycrystalline materials from an initial dataset of just five experimentally gathered 3D polycrystalline microstructures. We demonstrate the utility of PolyMicros by zero-shot solving several long standing challenges related to accelerating 3D experimental microscopy including reconstruction from partial observations for accelerated serial sections and reconstruction from partial statistics for 2D to 3D dimensionality expansion. Finally, we make both our models and datasets openly available to the community.

title: High-performance Fe-based superalloys designed via large language models and knowledge graphs
abstract: Fe-based superalloys are indispensable in high-temperature load-bearing components, yet simultaneous optimization of strength and ductility remains difficult due to the reliance on empirical design. Herein, a closed-loop design methodology is developed for Fe-based superalloys and experimentally validated by integrating large language model-driven knowledge extraction, knowledge graph-based semantic descriptors, multimodal property prediction, Bayesian active learning, and experimental verification. Composition-, processing-, and property-related entities and relations are extracted from the literature, organized into a materials knowledge graph, and encoded into semantic descriptors using domain-adaptive RoBERTa pretraining and graph representation learning. After fusion with structured descriptors, the surrogate models achieve an R2 of 0.96 for tensile strength prediction and improve elongation prediction from R2 values of 0.74 to 0.79. Bayesian optimization enables efficient exploration of the design space and leads to a new Fe-based superalloy with a room-temperature tensile strength of ∼1200 MPa, a total elongation of ∼47.5%, a strength-ductility product exceeding 50 GPa·%, and a yield strength of ∼900 MPa at 700 °C. The methodology provides an effective route for multi-objective alloy design and accelerated discovery in metallic material systems.

title: Predicting glass-forming ability in binary alloys by machine learning
abstract: Predicting metallic glass-forming ability (GFA) through machine learning has been challenging. Among the reasons for the challenge are limited, biased and inconsistent experimental data, binary vs continuous labeling, and limited feature representation particularly for multicomponent alloys. To address these challenges, we restrict the problem to binary alloys and base the training data on experiments spanning a representative fraction of ∼ 20% of binary alloys, which have been synthesized through sputtering and its atomic structure characterized. Consistent in quality and sufficient quantity of binary sputtering data with continuously labeled GFA quantified in the critical cooling rates (Rc) are constructed, and Physically Informed features based on atomic size, crystal mismatch, Miedema-based mixing enthalpy, and melting temperature are employed to describe the alloy in terms of its Rc. Using the Physically Informed features, the random forest model predicts the critical cooling rate with a mean absolute percentage error of ∼18% (MAPE in log₁₀ (Rc) space), compared to a simple benchmark model reaching a MAPE of 28%. However, attempts to use this binary model to predict Rc in ternary alloys are ineffective; using the ML model trained on binary data to predict Rc in ternary alloys results in a MAPE of ∼36% for sputtered ternary alloys and ∼ 89% for ternary BMG formers. Such poor performance suggests that the mixing complexity in ternary alloys is not captured in binary alloys. Overall, we argue that while addressing previous challenges in predicting GFA through ML, the models achieve statistically improved predictive performance while retaining a physically interpretable feature set. However, the achieved predictions remain coarse, indicating additional limitations (e.g., label uncertainty, missing higher-order mixing descriptors, process dependence, etc.) that constrain precise Rc prediction. Most fundamentally, the discreteness of atoms remains the limiting factor from using ML strategies to precisely predict glass-forming ability of alloys.

title: Interfacial segregation-driven machine learning: discovery of synergistic strength-ductility-high resistivity in titanium alloys
abstract: High electrical resistivity is crucial for minimizing eddy-current losses in metallic components operating under high-frequency magnetic fields, yet traditional strategies that rely on massive solute additions to elevate resistivity inevitably deteriorate mechanical integrity. Here, we established a new machine-learning driven high-throughput framework, which enables chemical boundary (CB) engineering in a model titanium alloy and achieves a favorable balance among these properties. The resultant alloy, Ti-2.5Zr-6.0Al-3.8Mn (wt.%), exhibits a favorable combination of ultimate tensile strength (∼1060 MPa), uniform elongation (∼8.5%) and electrical resistivity (∼1.94 μΩ·m). Through transmission electron microscopy, first-principles calculations, and Semi-discrete variational Peierls-Nabarro (SDVPN) analysis, we reveal that Mn-enriched CBs near the α/β interfaces lower the stacking-fault energies and intrinsic lattice resistance of pyramidal-Ⅱ <c+a> dislocations. The resulting activation of <c>-component dislocations improves c-axis strain accommodation and sustains strain hardening, thereby contributing to the simultaneous achievement of high strength and uniform elongation. Meanwhile, Mn enrichment induces localized magnetic moments and electrostatic potential gradients that provide additional electron-scattering centers, thereby contributing to the high electrical resistivity. This strategy integrates the advances in machine-learning and high-throughput sampling, providing a framework for the design of novel multifunctional structural metallic materials.

title: Learning lattice Kinetic Monte Carlo stochastic surface dynamics with Deep Generative Adversarial Networks
abstract: We show that Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) may be fruitfully exploited to learn stochastic dynamics, surrogating traditional models while capturing thermal fluctuations. Specifically, we showcase the application to a two-dimensional, many-particle system, focusing on surface-step fluctuations and on the related time-dependent roughness. After the construction of a dataset based on Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations, a conditional GAN is trained to propagate the state of the system stochastically in time, allowing the generation of new sequences with a reduced computational cost by approximately 40 times in the prototypical case considered here. Modifications with respect to standard GANs, which facilitate convergence and increase accuracy, are discussed. The trained network is demonstrated to quantitatively reproduce equilibrium and kinetic properties, including scaling laws, with deviations of a few percent from the exact value. Extrapolation limits and future perspectives are critically discussed.

title: InfinityEBSD : Metrics-guided infinite-size EBSD map generation with diffusion models
abstract: Materials performance is deeply linked to their microstructures, which govern key properties such as strength, durability, and fatigue resistance. EBSD is a major technique for characterizing these microstructures, but acquiring large EBSD maps suitable for computational modeling remains slow, costly, and often limited to small regions. In this work, we introduce InfinityEBSD, a diffusion-based method for generating monophase realistic EBSD maps of arbitrary size, conditioned on physically meaningful microstructural metrics. This approach supports two primary use cases: extending small experimental EBSD maps to arbitrary sizes, and generating entirely new maps directly from statistical descriptors, without any input map. Conditioning is achieved through eight microstructural descriptors, including grain size, grain perimeter, grain inertia ratio, coordination number and disorientation angle distribution, allowing the model to generate maps that are both visually realistic and physically interpretable. A patch-wise geometric extension strategy ensures spatial continuity across grains, enabling the model to produce large-scale EBSD maps while maintaining coherent grain boundaries and orientation transitions. The generated maps can also be exported as valid Channel Text Files (CTF) for immediate post-processing and analysis in software such as MTEX or simulation environments like DIGIMU®. We quantitatively validate our results by comparing distributions of the guiding metrics before and after generation, showing that the model respects the statistical targets while introducing morphological diversity. InfinityEBSD demonstrates that diffusion models, guided by physical metrics, can bridge the gap between synthetic and realistic materials representation, paving the way for future developments such as 3D realistic microstructure generation from 2D data.

title: Atomic-scale insights into the exceptional pinning effect of the K bubbles on W grain boundary
abstract: The application of tungsten (W) as plasma-facing materials (PFMs) in nuclear fusion reactors is limited by its low recrystallization temperature (RCT) and significant grain growth at elevated temperatures. Potassium (K)-doped W exhibits remarkably enhanced thermal stability due to nanoscale K bubbles, yet the atomic-scale pinning mechanism remains unclear. In this study, a high-precision neuroevolution potential (NEP) for the W-K system was developed using machine learning, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were performed to elucidate the unique pinning effect of the K bubbles on grain boundary (GB) migration. Our findings reveal that K bubbles exhibit distinct pinning characteristics compared to solid second-phase particles. Through quantification of GB migration velocity changes before and after the K bubble incorporation, the average pinning forces exerted by bubbles of different sizes were calculated, all of which were found to significantly exceed the maximum pinning forces predicted by classical Zener theory for solid particles of equivalent dimensions. The exceptional pinning capability is attributed to the high deformability of K bubbles, which exhibit substantial elongation and surface wrinkling during GB interactions, consequently expanding the contact area and amplifying pinning effectiveness. The findings lead to the proposition of a "deformation-enhanced pinning" mechanism that fundamentally accounts for the remarkable grain growth suppression achieved by trace K doping (<100 ppm). This work provides crucial theoretical guidance for designing advanced PFMs with superior thermal stability, paving the way for developing next-generation fusion materials.

title: Interfacial atomic vibration: A key dynamic characteristic for heterogeneous nucleation substrates
abstract: Heterogeneous nucleation during metal solidification is a key pathway for achieving grain refinement. However, due to the challenges in experimentally probing the solid-liquid interface, the underlying atomistic mechanisms remain unclear. Although classical lattice matching theories provide a framework for geometric compatibility, the static rigid models inherently neglect the strong atomic dynamics characteristic of high-temperature interfaces. In this study, ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) with on-the-fly machine learning force field (MLFF) is applied to evaluate the templating efficiency of different potential substrates for Al alloys. The templating efficiency is defined here as the capability to induce structural ordering within the pre-nucleation layer (PNL). The results show that a deep interfacial potential well (Ew) provides the necessary driving force to localize liquid atoms, whereas excessive atomic vibrations spatially disrupt this ordering process. The effect of temperature prompts the integration of interface dynamics into geometric mismatch. The dynamic stability is the main prerequisite for the initial PNL formation near the liquidus, and the epitaxial growth of PNL into stable nuclei is constrained by the accumulated lattice strain as the temperature decreases. Based on this dynamic-static mechanism and engineering considerations, a (Ta, Ti)B2/Al3Ta substrate is designed, which achieves significant grain refinement in Al-Si alloys. These findings deepen the understanding of heterogeneous nucleation and highlight interfacial dynamics as an important factor for the design of nucleation substrates.

title: Small features, big impact: Influence of overlooked microstructural features on high-entropy alloy predictions
abstract: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) exhibit a range of superior properties, making them attractive candidates for advanced engineering applications. However, their design and optimization remain challenging due to the complex interactions among multiple alloying elements. Machine learning (ML) has emerged as a powerful approach for accelerating the discovery of HEAs with tailored properties. In this study, ML models were employed to predict the hardness of AlCrFeNiTi HEAs across a broad compositional space. By incorporating microstructural knowledge into dataset construction, a more representative and physically informed training set was established. The influences of individual alloying elements on phase stability and microstructure evolution were systematically analyzed, providing a solid foundation for accurate predictions. Notably, the omission of minor microstructural features, such as nanoscale precipitates that occur only within limited compositional ranges, was found to markedly degrade prediction accuracy. We demonstrate a simple yet effective way or strategy to identify these critical features by analyzing compositions associated with the largest prediction deviations. Incorporating a small number of representative compositions containing these features significantly improved model performance. Beyond enhanced predictive capability, this approach also yielded mechanistic insights into the strengthening roles of specific elements in HEAs. These findings underscore the importance of integrating microstructural understanding into ML-driven alloy design to enable more reliable and efficient materials development.

title: Low-dimensional ruddlesden-popper anti-perovskites: a promising platform for flexible and high-performance solid-state batteries
abstract: The development of solid-state batteries demands solid-state electrolytes (SSEs) with high ionic conductivity, broad electrochemical windows, and mechanical flexibility. However, few materials meet all these criteria. In recent years, low-dimensional perovskite materials have demonstrated unique properties in frontier fields such as optoelectronics and catalysis, and typically exhibit better performance than three-dimensional materials. Nevertheless, their research and application in the SSE field remain in infancy. Herein, we used a low dimensional Ruddlesden Popper (RP) Li3n+1OnBrn+1 (n ∈ [1–5, ∞]) anti-perovskite SSE as the model system, combined with machine learning molecular dynamics (MLMD) simulation and first principles calculations to systematically investigate its thermal stability, electrochemical stability, mechanical stability, as well as electronic structure, mechanical properties, ion diffusion behavior, and defect characteristics, and analyzed the variation of these properties with n value. The results demonstrate that this series of materials exhibits outstanding thermal, electrochemistry and mechanical stability, a wide bandgap exceeding 5 eV, low defect formation energy, unique structural flexibility, and low ionic migration energy barriers ranging from 0.02 to 0.26 eV. Interestingly, we found that the n value serves as a key descriptor for regulating the properties of RP materials: as n decreases, material stability progressively increases, the overall bandgap widens, the structural flexibility gradually improves, and the ion diffusion ability gradually improves. Further mechanistic analysis revealed that soft phonon modes at rock-salt layer interfaces within the RP materials facilitate rapid two-dimensional diffusion of lithium ions along the interfaces. This study offers new insights for designing high-performance flexible low-dimensional SSE materials.

title: Local chemical inhomogeneities in Al-containing multi-principal element alloys explored by utilizing an ab-initio based approach
abstract: Multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs) exhibit rich local chemical inhomogeneities (LCIs), such as chemical ordering, elemental segregation, and composition undulation, arising from complex physicochemical interactions. Understanding and controlling LCIs are crucial for tailoring the properties of MPEAs. A novel method based on machine learning algorithm is therefore proposed for quantifying composition undulation. Combined with Warren-Cowley parameters, evolution of LCIs in Ti-Al-Nb-Zr MPEAs was comprehensively investigated through Monte Carlo simulations based on cluster expansion. The results reveal that Al-Zr atomic pairs show the strongest bonding preference and promote the formation of AlZr-rich domains at low temperatures. As exemplified by the recently well-studied Ti58Al13Nb14Zr15 alloy, the AlZr-rich domain is energetically unstable and transforms into a hexagonal structure upon structural relaxation, corresponding to the experimentally observed α2 phase. Under low Zr content, a synergistic interaction is observed among Ti, Al, and Nb. As the temperature decreases, they cooperatively rearrange to form a TiAlNb-ordered phase. Because of the identical compositions of the parent and the ordered phases, the microstructure is characterized by an absence of compositional fluctuations for these alloys. In turn, increasing Al and Nb promotes chemical ordering and raises the order-disorder transition temperature, whereas higher Al and Zr concentrations enhance composition undulation and elevate the phase separation temperature. Comparison to experimental data suggests that the simulations yield reliable predictions on the microstructural evolutions. These findings advance the understanding of LCIs evolution in Ti-Al-Nb-Zr MPEAs, offering valuable insights into composition-microstructure relationships and guiding the design of advanced MPEAs.

title: Denoising diffusion probabilistic model-based tabular data augmentation for improved phase classification of high-entropy alloys
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) offer significant potential for accelerating materials discovery. However, their practical application is often limited by data scarcity. Conventional data augmentation techniques, such as rule-based data transformations and generative models, fall short in producing realistic and diverse synthetic data. This study pioneers the adoption of the denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) as a novel generative framework to address these challenges in the context of high-entropy alloy (HEA) phase prediction. By incorporating DDPM-generated synthetic samples into the training process, the phase classification model achieves significantly improved prediction accuracy and generalizability, as validated across a diverse set of experimentally synthesized samples and literature-collected data. To further evaluate its data generation effectiveness, DDPM was systematically benchmarked against two state-of-the-art augmentation techniques: Adaptive Synthetic Sampling (ADASYN) and the Conditional Tabular Generative Adversarial Network (CTGAN). Comparative results demonstrate that DDPM consistently outperforms both methods, exhibiting superior capability in generating high-quality synthetic data. Overall, this work highlights DDPM as a highly promising generative framework for materials informatics, paving the way for more effective data-driven materials discovery.

title: Discovery of intrinsically high-hardness high-entropy carbides
abstract: The vast compositional space poses significant challenge for discovering high-entropy carbides (HECs) with high intrinsic hardness through traditional trial-and-error methods and computational approaches. To address this, high-throughput (HTP) fabrication and characterization techniques have been developed for HECs, which enables high-efficiency acquisition of fundamental data. Based on these data, a sequential machine learning (ML) workflow was constructed to predict intrinsic hardness property of single-phase HECs. Guided by the ML results, a series of novel equimolar and non-equimolar HEC bulk materials with nanohardness exceeding 36 GPa were designed and successfully fabricated. It was illustrated that the atomic volume mismatch is a key factor governing single-phase formability and hardness of HECs. Smaller atomic volume mismatch favors single-phase formation due to reduction of lattice distortion energy, while larger atomic volume mismatch increases intrinsic hardness through enhancing lattice distortion. In addition, the valence electron concentration (VEC) affects hardness of HEC by modulating the covalent bond strength of metal-carbon bonds. The strategy proposed in this study, which integrates HTP feature acquisition, ML phase prediction, and property-oriented material design, can be widely applied to develop a broad range of HECs.

title: Machine-learning prediction for solid–liquid interfacial properties from micrographs in Al–Cu and Fe–Mn alloys
abstract: An approach is proposed for experimentally determining the solid–liquid interfacial free energy (γ0) and the anisotropy parameter (ϵ). In this approach, γ0 and ϵ are predicted by inputting micrographs of as-cast microstructures into a convolutional neural network (CNN). The CNN was trained exclusively on datasets generated by a quantitative phase-field model to establish the linkage between the interfacial properties and as-cast microstructural patterns. To assess the practicality of this approach, γ0 and ϵ were predicted from experimental micrographs of an Al–3.5 mass%Cu alloy and an Fe–14 mass%Mn alloy. The average predicted values were γ0=0.135±0.019Jm−2 and ϵ=0.0106±0.0029for the Al–Cu alloy, and γ0=0.206±0.012Jm−2 and ϵ=0.0213±0.0024 for the Fe–Mn alloy. These results show good agreement with the literature values. Systematic analysis of a large-scale phase-field dataset further reveals that reliable inference of γ0 and ϵ emerges only through coupled variations of multiple morphological descriptors rather than any single dominant metric, a relationship consistently reproduced by the CNN predictions. These findings indicate that the present approach is both practical and promising for evaluating solid–liquid interfacial properties from microstructural observations.

title: Role of dislocation locking and unlocking in the yield strength anomaly of γ-TiAl revealed by machine-learning moment tensor potential
abstract: The yield stress anomaly (YSA) is a commonly observed phenomenon in ordered intermetallics in which the yield stress increases with temperature over an intermediate temperature range. Understanding this effect is key to engineering the properties of intermetallic materials used in high temperature, high stress applications, such as jet engines. However, the fundamental mechanisms of YSA in γ-TiAl are still not understood. In this work, we leverage a newly developed machine learning interatomic potential based on the Moment Tensor Potential formalism to perform molecular statics and dynamics simulations of dislocations in γ-TiAl. We observe that, analogous to the Kear–Wilsdorf locks in Ni3Al, 〈01̄1] screw superdislocations in γ-TiAl can undergo locking through cross-slip, transforming a glissile planar core into a sessile non-planar core. Analysis of the transition state provides evidence that this mechanism is consistent with the YSA. The frequency of cross-slip is found to increase at elevated temperatures, consistent with a thermally-activated locking mechanism. This core transformation involves the conversion of a complex stacking fault in the planar core to a more stable superlattice intrinsic stacking fault in the non-planar core. We also find that the locking mechanism can be modified in off-stoichiometric γ-TiAl, suggesting alloying strategies to tune the YSA.

title: Design of hydrogen-resistant high-strength medium-Mn steels via Pareto active learning
abstract: A multi-objective optimization strategy based on Pareto active learning was employed to design martensitic medium-Mn steels with simultaneously enhanced ultimate tensile strength (UTS) and hydrogen embrittlement (HE) resistance. A high-dimensional search space comprising over 400,000 candidate compositions was constructed by incorporating microalloying elements (Ti, V, and Mo) identified via density functional theory as effective for enhancing HE resistance. Starting from only five initial datasets, Gaussian Process Regression-based surrogate models were iteratively refined through active learning cycles using newly acquired experimental data, progressively balancing exploration and exploitation. After five iterations, the optimized G6–1 steel (Fe-6.2Mn-0.21C-0.3Si-0.18Mo-0.19V-0.02Ti-0.003B (wt%)) achieved a UTS of 2336 MPa with superior HE resistance, representing an approximately 33% improvement in the combined strength–HE resistance metric. Machine learning–based correlation analysis revealed that austenite stability, characterized by unstable stacking fault energy (USF energy), plays a dominant role in enhancing HE resistance by suppressing the transformation of retained austenite into martensite. Furthermore, the combined addition of V and Mo exhibited a synergistic effect on HE resistance by enhancing the trapping efficiency of MC carbides, which originates from an increased concentration of C vacancies in (V,Mo) carbides due to the reduced C-vacancy formation energy induced by Mo substitution.

title: Flow matching-based computational reconstruction framework for multiphase materials and performance evaluation
abstract: Computational reconstruction of heterogeneous material microstructure is essential for pore-scale modeling and establishing structure–property relationships. Deep learning-based reconstruction methods offer advantages in efficiency, but they struggle with reconstruction accuracy for multiphase microstructure and lack interpretability. Flow matching has emerged as a promising solution, but its application requires a substantial dataset and remains limited to 2D image synthesis. To address these challenges, we propose a novel flow matching-based reconstruction framework for multiphase microstructure. Our method formulates microstructure reconstruction as solving an ordinary differential equation, providing a deterministic and interpretable generative trajectory. Specifically, an optimal transport path is adopted to establish the deterministic trajectory from noisy samples to realistic microstructures. A neural network model is designed to regress target velocity field that governs the trajectory, enabling precise modeling of the deterministic trajectory. The Euler method integration is used to solute the ordinary differential equation, ensuring stable and efficient microstructure reconstruction. The proposed framework is evaluated across three representative multiphase materials (NMC electrodes, Ni-YSZ anodes, and cement paste) through visualization, statistical parameters, and physical property analyses. Experimental results demonstrate that generated microstructures are visually and statistically consistent with target microstructures, accurately capturing their functional characteristics. This work establishes flow matching as an effective approach for generating high-quality statistically equivalent virtual microstructure, providing a reliable digital foundation for property prediction and material design.

title: Atomistic modeling of polymorphism in iron using an explicitly magnetic machine-learned interatomic potential
abstract: While several efforts have been made to incorporate spin dynamics explicitly into interatomic potentials for magnetic materials, they have typically been unable to account for polymorphism and the change in magnetic interaction with structure. Those that do have had difficulties in reproducing the experimentally or theoretically known properties of multiple phases in dynamic simulation. Using the Rapid Artificial Neural Network (RANN) machine-learned interatomic potential as a template, we introduce magnetically coupled structural fingerprints in addition to the typical non-magnetic descriptors. These are used with a first principles database for pure iron to train an explicitly magnetic RANN potential which reproduces a number of experimentally observed and theoretically calculated properties of both the ferritic and austenitic phases of iron. Critically, these include the magnon spectrum of BCC iron, the demagnetization and Curie Temperature of ferrite, and phase transitions with increasing temperature, including the presence of the high temperature BCC phase. This provides not only a machine-learned interatomic potential which can be used in LAMMPS to study inherently magnetic, mechanical, and thermodynamic properties of iron, but also a template for the creation of magnetic MLIPs for other materials and alloys.

title: Crossover from sluggish to accelerated diffusion in multi-principal element alloys induced by lattice distortion
abstract: Sluggish diffusion and lattice distortion are core factors in multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs) that are responsible for their unique properties. Nonetheless, the existence and mechanisms of sluggish diffusion remain controversial. In this study, we reveal the intricate interplay between diffusion and lattice distortion using equilibrium Monte Carlo (MC) and kinetic Monte Carlo (kMC) simulations driven by a Graph Neural Network (GNN) model that captures local atomic environment-dependent energy states and path-dependent transition rates. Our results demonstrate that lattice distortion significantly elevates equilibrium vacancy concentrations in MPEAs. Integrating insights from vacancy concentration and kMC-derived diffusivity, we identify a crossover in the self-diffusion coefficient of MPEAs as a function of the degree of lattice distortion. Sluggish diffusion is observed in systems with moderate distortion, where increased vacancy concentration, accelerated vacancy jump frequency, and stronger correlation effects compete. Unexpectedly, a higher degree of lattice distortion leads to accelerated instead of sluggish diffusion due to the weak correlation effect. Our findings establish the critical connection between structural features and kinetic properties in MPEAs, offering a foundation for designing high-performance alloys with tailored kinetics by strategically tuning structural characteristics within the vast compositional space.

title: Slip- and shuffling-based cross-slip mechanisms of c+a screw dislocations in magnesium
abstract: Cross-slip of c+a screw dislocations is a key process governing non-basal dislocation multiplication and ductility in magnesium, yet its atomistic mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here, using nudged elastic band calculations with a neural network potential (NNP), we identify two distinct constriction-free cross-slip mechanisms between pyramidal II (Pyr. II) and pyramidal I (Pyr. I) core states: a slip-based mechanism dominated by collective atomic glide and a shuffling-based mechanism enabled by localized atomic rearrangements intrinsic to the Pyr. II stacking fault structure. The energetic origin of these mechanisms is first clarified through Pyr. II stacking fault migration, where the slip-based mechanism involves severe interlayer atomic overlap and has an NNP-predicted barrier of 127 mJ/m2, whereas the shuffling-based mechanism avoids such overlap and is nearly barrierless. The NNP-predicted MEPs show that the same distinction governs both two- and three-dimensional c+a cross-slip, with the shuffling-based mechanism markedly reducing the zero-stress barrier. In the three-dimensional analysis, a 2D cross-sectional energy descriptor reveals cross-slip as a wave-like propagation of local two-dimensional core transformations and refines the interpretation of jog-pair nucleation. These results establish an atomistically resolved framework for modeling c+a cross-slip in magnesium and suggest analogous mechanisms in a broad range of hexagonal close-packed metals.

title: Optimizing intrinsic strength–plasticity synergy for refractory high entropy alloy by chemical bonding engineering
abstract: Developing strength‑plasticity synergy in refractory high‑entropy alloys (RHEAs) is challenging due to their vast composition space and intrinsic low ductility. Here, we demonstrate a machine learning‑assisted bond engineering method to improve plasticity while maintaining high strength at both room temperature and 1200 °C, using the WMoTaNbV system as a model. Through statistical correlation of bonding states with intrinsic mechanical properties and electronic structure analysis, ductile bonding characteristics (bonding states near the Fermi level and low –ICOHP) and strengthening bonding characteristics (opposite features) were identified. By machine learning‑guided bond distribution regulation, the W₂₃Mo₂Ta₃₅Nb₅V₃₅ alloy was designed and experimentally validated, achieving a high room‑temperature yield strength of ∼1.52 GPa, an ultimate compressive strength of 2.8 GPa, and a fracture strain of ∼24 %, which far exceeds all the literature reports. The bonding mechanism responsible for strengthening and toughening was further analyzed via in‑situ tensile experiments and atomistic simulations. This bond‑directed design strategy goes beyond conventional composition‑based screening by revealing the electronic origin of the strength‑plasticity balance, providing a rational basis for fine‑tuning mechanical properties in RHEAs.

title: Concentration-dependent suppression of thermal anisotropy in 4H-SiC by nitrogen doping
abstract: Nitrogen (N) doping is a standard and well-established strategy for achieving n-type conductivity in 4H-silicon carbide (SiC), which has enabled extensive use in power electronic devices and other emerging applications. However, the effect of N doping on thermal transport properties, especially the anisotropy behavior governing electronic devices cooling, remains poorly understood. In this work, a unified neural network potential (NNP) is developed to elucidate the atomistic origins of concentration-dependent thermal conductivity (к) anisotropy behavior in N-doped SiC. The simulation results indicate that N doping markedly suppresses the anisotropy of к. At the microscopic level, strong phonon localization and polarization disorder induced by doping atoms enhance phonon scattering and shorten phonon relaxation times. Different from the predominantly in-plane polarization of low-frequency phonons in pristine SiC, N doping enhances out-of-plane polarization components and reduces the anisotropy of к. The in-depth microscopic understanding of N doping modulated thermal transport in 4H-SiC provides significant insight into the thermal management of n-type SiC electronic devices.

title: Strain-gradient-driven decoupling of thermal suppression from anisotropy in β-Ga2O3
abstract: Strain gradients, ubiquitous in flexible devices and epitaxial nanostructures, are a major blind spot for thermal transport in \b{eta}-Ga2O3. We establish that strain gradient unlocks a thermal conductivity (k) suppression mechanism fundamentally more potent than uniform strain: moderate uniaxial gradients (0.6%/nm) suppress k by 32-37% (27-30%) in thin films (nanowires), intensifying to 43.3% with biaxial gradients. This reduction far exceeds that from equivalent uniform strain and surpasses benchmark materials like silicon and BAs. Critically, a surprising decoupling emerges: while 3% uniform strain alters thermal anisotropy by ~25%, strain gradient strongly suppresses k with preserving this ratio. Mechanistically, strain gradients-induced symmetry breaking and enhanced mode coupling anisotropically activate forbidden scattering channels, making gradient-driven scattering dominant over intrinsic phonon scattering below 6.25 THz. These findings redefine non-uniform strain from a parasitic flaw into a powerful design tool for engineering thermal isolation and heat flux in next-generation flexible and high-power \b{eta}-Ga2O3 electronics.

title: Phase crossover enables large work output and low thermal hysteresis in shape memory actuation
abstract: Achieving both large work output and low thermal hysteresis in TiNi-based shape memory actuators remains challenging due to their inherent trade-off: the B2–B19′ martensitic transformation provides large transformation strain but high thermal hysteresis, while the B2–B19 transformation yields low thermal hysteresis but limited strain. Here, we propose a design strategy to target compositions near the phase crossover between B19′ and B19 martensites, where both phases can coexist. Combined with machine learning-assisted multi-objective optimization of processing conditions, this approach led to the development of a Ti50Ni41.3Cu8Hf0.3Co0.4 alloy exhibiting a low thermal hysteresis about 10 °C and a work output exceeding 30 MJ/m3, outperforming most TiNi-based shape memory alloys. The finely tuned composition improves lattice compatibility to reduce thermal hysteresis, while the B2–B19′ transformation occurred under actuation stress enables large recoverable strain. Additionally, grain refinement and residual dislocations enhance strength, thereby enabling the alloy to realize its full work output potential. This strategy, which integrates phase diagram insights with data-driven materials design, provides an efficient pathway for discovering new phase-change materials with superior functional performance.

title: Data-driven determination of the critical inclusion characteristic size in powder metallurgy superalloys
abstract: The fatigue life reliability of powder metallurgy (PM) superalloy turbine disks is critically important for ensuring stable operation and service safety of aero-engines. In-situ SEM observations demonstrated that inclusion variations between 1.5 and 2.5 μm only induced damage without causing fracture, while low-cycle fatigue tests revealed that the fluctuation in the fatigue life of PM Udimet 720Li primarily originated from manufacturing-induced inclusion size variations between 5 and 84 μm. The complex morphology of nonmetallic inclusions remains a major obstacle to accurately identifying the critical size that dictates the fatigue life of PM superalloys. Analysis of crystal plasticity finite element demonstrates that the inclusion shape factor significantly influences the variation amplitude of the fatigue crack initiation indicator parameter(FIP, Pac). The inclusion area dominates over shape factor in governing the accumulation of plastic strain. This work proposes a novel physics-informed machine learning model, termed CICS-Transformer, which effectively captures the nonlinear coupling between inclusion characteristics and FIP and enables uncertainty-aware predictions with high accuracy and reliability under data-scarce conditions. Our FIP-predicting neural network generated a 3D heatmap showing D, η, L,and Max Pac relationships, reducing prediction errors by 15.7% and 3.2% versus two traditional models. The integrated critical inclusion characteristic size prediction framework, characterized by its interpretability and generalization capability, underscores the value of combining physics-informed prior knowledge with advanced deep learning methodologies in deepening the understanding of alloy damage tolerance theory. Furthermore, it provides a reference for the service safety assessment of next-generation turbine disks.

title: A unified predictive framework for α′ precipitation in Fe–Cr–Al alloys based on effective diffusion length: From dense-cascade irradiation to thermal aging
abstract: Quantitative prediction of α′ precipitation in Fe–Cr–Al alloys across the several-orders-of-magnitude dose-rate gap between ion and neutron irradiation is essential for accident-tolerant fuel (ATF) cladding design, yet no unified framework exists. Twelve Fe–(10–22)Cr–(0–14)Al (at.%) model alloys were self-ion irradiated at 350 °C over three dose rates (8×10−6–8×10−4 dpa/s) and three doses (0.24–1.44 dpa) to construct an 84-condition atom probe tomography (APT) database. At the highest dose rate, a nucleation→growth→ballistic-dissolution-dominated transition was directly observed. Published irradiation and thermal-aging APT data were integrated, and a unified framework was developed using the effective diffusion length Leff, derived from Sizmann’s point-defect theory, as a physical compression variable. Leff compresses dose rate, dose, temperature, and time into a single scalar with no irradiation-type-specific fitting parameters. Machine learning models employing only three variables — Cr, Al, and log10(Leff) — yielded cross-validated R2=0.56–0.82 for the four target α′ metrics (number density Nd, mean radius R̄, volume fraction Vf, and Cr concentration CCrin). Leave-Neutron-Out validation, in which all neutron data were withheld from training, demonstrated that Vf (R2=0.69) and log10(Nd) (R2=0.58) can be extrapolated from ion-irradiation and thermal-aging data alone. In contrast, R̄ and CCrin could not be extrapolated, cleanly separating the diffusion-controlled aspects of α′ precipitation that Leff captures from the irradiation-type-dependent ballistic-mixing contribution that it does not encode. Partial dependence analysis revealed a non-monotonic effect whereby ∼5 at.% Al addition promotes rather than suppresses α′ formation across the entire Leff range, identifying an Al composition window to be avoided in ATF cladding alloys.

title: Revealing the shock-induced complex phase transformations of tin and their impacts on spallation
abstract: Spallation, a critical mode of dynamic fracture, remains a central focus in the study of material response under extreme conditions. While widely studied in common metals, the spallation of tin (Sn), a group IV element exhibiting multiple solid phases along the shock-Hugoniot, presents significant challenges due to its complex pressure–temperature phase diagram. Such complexity hinders both experimental characterization and the development of reliable interatomic potentials for atomistic simulations. Consequently, the phase transition pathways and their influence on spallation in Sn remain poorly understood. In this work, we employ non-equilibrium molecular dynamics simulations using a first-principles accuracy machine learning potential to simulate the dynamic response of Sn at strain rates down to ∼6×109s−1, which is comparable to experiments. Our simulations successfully capture critical behaviors such as shock-induced phase transitions and melting, and reproduce their experimental shock pressures. Meanwhile, the results clearly elucidate the β-to-bct transition pathway, revealing a two-stage mechanism mediated by an intermediate simple-hexagonal phase. Furthermore, we identify two distinct dynamic behaviors along the loading-unloading thermodynamic pathway: shock-induced kinetic metastable cold melting below the equilibrium melting point and phase-transition-mediated release amorphization. These behaviors are shown to originate from the large differences in the slopes of the melting lines between adjacent solid phases. Overall, the findings provide atomistic-scale evidence directly linking phase transformations to spallation failure, offering new insights into the fundamental physics of dynamic fracture in Sn.

title: High-throughput screening of oxidation kinetics in a combinatorial library of Ni-Co-Fe-Cr(-Al)-based superalloys
abstract: A combinatorial library of one hundred Ni-Co-Fe-Cr(-Al)-based superalloys is synthesized from blends of four basis alloys via powder-blown directed energy deposition: Ni-based INCONEL® 625, Co-based HAYNES® 25, Fe-based stainless steel 316L, and a commercial Ni–Co–Cr–Al–Y bond coat. One hundred total alloys across four monolithic 5×5 alloy arrays are each oxidized in air at 870 or 950 °C for up to 9 days. Oxide scales are characterized by X-ray diffraction (XRD) to quantify phase fractions and infer growth kinetics. Parallelized alloy fabrication and oxidation enable semi-automated XRD measurement and pattern refinement, accelerating characterization by ∼5× relative to serial mass gain or cross-section thickness measurements. This scalable experimental framework screens a large quaternary composition space using a logarithmic-growth kinetic constant, K0, as a quantitative metric for oxide scale evolution. XRD-derived K0 shows good agreement with a traditional cross-section approach; correlations between K0 and composition also reproduce established oxidation trends in superalloys. At 950 °C, Al additions reduce K0 and oxide scale thickness (after 9 days) by up to an order of magnitude. The transition between Type II and Type III oxidation occurs at ∼5 at. % Al, and a total concentration of Al + Cr ≥ 29 at. % is recommended for alumina-forming superalloy coatings. A Gaussian process regression (GPR) surrogate model is constructed to predict oxidation-resistant compositions, identifying an optimized alloy candidate near binary IN625 + 40 wt. % Ni–Co–Cr–Al–Y; corresponding to an overall composition of Ni–20Cr–9Co–5Al–5Mo–3Fe–2Nb (wt. %).
